title: Higher-Order Derivatives Do Not Accelerate the Computation of Fixed Points
summary: The Picard iteration converges to the unique fixed point of a $q$-contractive operator at a linear rate $q^N$, and a lower bound with an affine construction shows that no deterministic method querying only operator values can do better. But what about higher-order methods that query derivatives? A single Jacobian evaluation reveals an affine map entirely, so the affine construction says nothing about higher-order methods. In this work, we show that finite-order derivative information still does not accelerate the worst-case complexity for smooth contractive fixed-point computation. This…
